title: Nine o'clock bell and the old N. John house
summary: Children were off the street by the nine o'clock bell, enforced by family; he places the old N. John house and the 9th Precinct.

blocks.x: When that bell rang, if you were out on the street, could any adult sort of accost you, tell you to go home? Or what would happen to you?

Well, they wouldn't have to do it. They could do it, but they wouldn't have to do it. Because I mean all the children was under that same fit. They had to be inside for nine o'clock. The bell started to ring at nine. I would say about five minutes to nine. It stopped at nine. But by the time it stopped, them kids were off the street. And when you saw children out after that hour, they'd be out with their parents. Some of their parents would have them.
You'd have to be out with an adult.
Yeah, I mean it wasn't a compolter law. It was a compolter family law. I mean the city didn't compol you to be off. But your people is the one that would put that law on you.
Where was the location of that N. John house?

That was on Maple between Boydette and Foyan. Yeah, that's all residential up there now. Yeah, that old N. John house stayed there for many years. Many of the old times, especially from Caldoun, can tell you about that old N. John house. The old N. John house and the old 9th Precinct. That's two old places they'd never forget. 9th Precinct and the Foyan John.
